messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: multiple container restarts in gpu-pool-12 (zone-us-west-2) detected. High memory growth during prefill stage. Auto-pager: @maya (oncall)
maya (oncall): acknowledged, looking. any obvious customer impact yet?
aj (eng): seeing repeated OOM on model-id: redwood/long-window-v1 during prefill. containers restart every ~90s on node gpu-12-07. logs show CUDA OOM then process exit. snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.50 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 2.00 GiB cached)
  File "/app/runtime/generations.py", line 242, in prefill
    kv_cache.grow(...)
```
kevin (ml-runtime): that model has dense KV growth with long-context prompts. looks like some requests are sending huge prefill windows (user context ~150k tokens).
opsbot: isolating node gpu-12-07 from serving pool (reason: repeated OOM). Traffic rerouted.
maya (oncall): good. start mitigation checklist: 1) isolate node (done) 2) pin fallback model / smaller context 3) apply temporary prefill cap 4) notify affected customers
aj (eng): live metrics: replica failures spiking 5xx for route /v1/generate:model=long-window-v1 from 04:12 - 04:18 UTC. estimate ~0.4% of total requests, but concentrated on 2 enterprise customers.
kevin (ml-runtime): recommend immediate config hotpatch: enforce prefill_token_limit=8192 at router layer for that model id + enable KV trimming (kv_trim_ratio=0.25) on serving runtime. This should stop runaway allocations quickly.
maya (oncall): can we hotpatch without a full deploy?
aj (eng): yes, router supports runtime overrides. pushing change now. patch: ```POST /admin/hotpatch
{
  "model_id": "redwood/long-window-v1",
  "overrides": {
    "prefill_token_limit": 8192,
    "kv_trim_ratio": 0.25
  }
}```
opsbot: hotpatch applied to region us-west-2 on 6/3 04:22 UTC. verified config present on edge routers.
kevin (ml-runtime): also started KV-cache eviction sweep on the node pool to reclaim cached states from largest sessions. monitoring GPU mem usage.
elena (customer-sre): looping in account teams for the two impacted customers (org-392, org-811). preparing a short customer note: "We observed transient failures for long-context requests; we applied temporary limits and are rolling a fix to prevent restarts. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation plan."
jack (support): created support tickets for both orgs (SUP-3219, SUP-3220) and added status note. Customers currently see transient 5xx and occasional stream drop; no data loss.
maya (oncall): rolling check: after fixes, node restarts stopped, OOMs reduced on remaining replicas. routing latency normalizing.
aj (eng): logs after hotpatch: OOM events dropped to 0 within 3 minutes. observed some degraded outputs for in-flight very-long sessions (they were truncated by prefill cap) — will surface to customers in notes.
kevin (ml-runtime): followups: - add per-tenant prefill telemetry (so a single noisy tenant doesn't blow kvcache) - add auto-prefill-shed policy when KV growth > threshold - longer term: model changes to stream prefill or sparse attention to reduce KV size.
elena (customer-sre): ETA to customers: initial message sent, follow-up RCA & permanent mitigation plan by EOD.
maya (oncall): final: on-call clear unless OOMs reappear. keeping watch for 30m. thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed for pager rotation: oncall cleared at 04:52 UTC.
